newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Sabena considers relocating pilots abroad.
newsitem.headline: Sabena considers relocating pilots abroad.

text.p: Belgian airline Sabena said on Tuesday it was considering relocating its pilots to a foreign country to avoid having to pay heavy Belgian social security levies and to save two billion francs ($64.9 million) a year.

"Social security costs are much higher in Belgium than in other European countries, which means we have to pay much more for our pilots to give them the same net wages," Sabena's spokesman Erik Sclep said.

Sclep added that Sabena would continue talks with the Belgian government, which has a narrow minority in the airline, and the governments of countries where it might relocate the pilots to before any decisions were taken.
"There have been plans to relocate to Switzerland but at this moment it is too early to give definite information about which country (Sabena) is considering," he said.
The relocation, known as the 'common crew management' plan, would involve around 500 pilots and aims to save the airline around two billion Belgian francs a year, Sclep said.
Sabena first considered this plan in 1995, but shelved it after unsuccessful results.
Paul Reutlinger, Sabena's chief executive who joined from shareholder Swissair, took up the idea again, Sclep added.
The Swiss airline owns a 49.5 percent stake in Sabena.
